raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Document that callers serialize sleep, wake, pause and resume operations, including across clients. This is the standalone split requested by @aoshen02 in https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/185, extracted from #58183.

## Claims

- Explain that `sleep(mode="wait")` completes after draining and worker sleep, while EngineCore can still process other control messages during the drain.
- State that overlapping control requests are unsupported and a client timeout does not establish the operation's outcome.
- Cover successful sleep completion and immediate/deferred worker failures using the existing engine test fixture.

## Validation

On standalone main `06e172b5cf8845c80c40a6eaaecbcbde3e38e8df` plus this change: **25 selected engine tests passed**. Applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy, passed.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "checkpoint or pause or sleep or kv_cache_release or wake_up or reject" -q -rs`

This documents existing behavior; it does not add runtime serialization or claim a before/after behavior fix. No new GPU benchmark was needed.

### Earlier integration evidence and contract correction from #58183

The combined revision `a2472393067b4e04e83cdb7bc3f93aa52c8a67fa` passed real HTTP request-draining, partial-wake and matching post-wake-output scenarios with insecure serialization disabled. The original report also recorded rejection of overlapping management transitions in that revision. That is historical behavior of the combined implementation; it is **not** a guarantee provided by this documentation-only control contract. This split requires callers to serialize operations, including across clients.

The later combined revision `c9171d7ad9eedd77d7633d5cdb0355018ff9b29a` passed 5 opt-in H20 GPU regression configurations (TP1/2/4 peer-to-peer and TP2/4 forced shared memory, three cycles each with Qwen3-0.6B), covering both partial-wake orders and repeated sleep. Those runs provide integration context for the documented call sequence, not evidence that concurrent control requests are now serialized internally.

The current branch's three targeted regression cases check successful drain-and-sleep completion, immediate worker failure and deferred worker failure in the existing engine fixture; together with the selected regressions, **25 tests passed**. Historical GPU scenarios from [#58183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58183) were not rerun for this documentation/test split.

## Details

The change is limited to `docs/features/sleep_mode.md`, the `EngineCore.sleep()` docstring/comment, and three existing-fixture regression cases. Related to #48311; CUDA checkpointing remains a separate change.

AI assistance: Codex implementation/validation and independent evaluator review.

@@ -16,6 +16,22 @@ Key benefits:
 !!! note
     For more information, see this [Blog Post](https://blog.vllm.ai/2025/10/26/sleep-mode.html).
 
+## Control request ordering
+
+The caller must serialize sleep, wake, pause, and resume operations for each
+engine, including requests from different clients. Wait for each operation to
+complete successfully before issuing the next one. With asynchronous Python
+APIs, await the operation; with HTTP APIs, wait for its successful response.
+
+`sleep(mode="wait")` waits for in-flight requests to finish and for worker sleep
+to complete before returning to the caller. This does not block EngineCore from
+handling other control requests while requests drain. Overlapping control
+operations are unsupported; the engine does not guarantee that it will reject
+them or execute them in the intended order. Coordinate multiple clients through
+a single controller or a shared lock. A timeout or disconnected client does not
+prove that the operation stopped; establish its outcome before issuing another
+control operation.
+
 ## Sleep levels
 
 Level 1 sleep will offload the model weights and discard the KV cache. The content of KV cache is forgotten. Level 1 sleep is good for sleeping and waking up the engine to run the same model again. The model weights are backed up in CPU memory. Please make sure there's enough CPU memory to store the model weights. Level 2 sleep will discard both the model weights and the KV cache (while the model's buffers are kept in CPU, like rope scaling tensors). The content of both the model weights and KV cache is forgotten. Level 2 sleep is good for sleeping and waking up the engine to run a different model or update the model, where previous model weights are not needed, e.g. RLHF weight update. Level 2 sleep is also useful when there is not enough CPU memory to back up the model weights, e.g. when a colocated trainer already uses CPU memory for offloading its own state; since nothing is backed up, restore the weights after waking up with `collective_rpc("reload_weights")`.

@@ -760,6 +760,43 @@ def _pausable_engine_core_proc() -> EngineCoreProc:
     return core
 
 
+def test_sleep_wait_completes_before_caller_wakes():
+    """The caller waits for draining and worker sleep before issuing wake."""
+    core = _pausable_engine_core_proc()
+    core.scheduler.has_requests.return_value = True
+    core._reset_caches = MagicMock()
+    future = core.sleep(mode="wait")
+    assert future is not None and not future.done()
+
+    core.model_executor.sleep.assert_not_called()
+    core.model_executor.wake_up.assert_not_called()
+
+    core.scheduler.has_requests.return_value = False
+    core._notify_idle_state_callbacks()
+    future.result()
+    core.model_executor.sleep.assert_called_once_with(1)
+    core.wake_up()
+    core.model_executor.wake_up.assert_called_once_with(None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("deferred", [False, True])
+def test_sleep_failure_propagates_to_caller(deferred):
+    core = _pausable_engine_core_proc()
+    core.scheduler.has_requests.return_value = deferred
+    core._reset_caches = MagicMock()
+    core.model_executor.sleep.side_effect = RuntimeError("injected sleep failure")
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="injected sleep failure"):
+        future = core.sleep(mode="wait")
+        if deferred:
+            core.scheduler.has_requests.return_value = False
+            core._notify_idle_state_callbacks()
+            future.result()
+    # The injected failure precedes worker mutation, so this retry is safe.
+    core.model_executor.sleep.side_effect = None
+    core.sleep(mode="wait")
+    assert core.model_executor.sleep.call_count == 2
+
+
